items.prompt: Your turn, on a new board. Tap every square the white pawn on d2 can move to. Not sure yet? Press a hint.
hints: Ask two questions: which squares ahead are empty, and which diagonal squares hold an enemy piece?
The pawn is on its starting square, so it has a two-square jump as well as a single step.
The pawn can walk to d3 and d4, and it can capture on c3 and on e3.
items.explain: The pawn is on its starting square with d3 and d4 empty, so it can step or jump. Enemy pieces stand on both forward diagonals, so it can capture either one.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the black pawn on e7 can move to.
hints: Check the colour first. Black pawns walk down the board.
The jump needs both squares ahead empty. Is e5 empty?
One step to e6, and two captures: the bishop on d6 and the knight on f6.
items.explain: A black pawn walks down the board. e6 is empty, but the white rook on e5 stops the two-square jump. The white bishop on d6 and the white knight on f6 stand on its forward diagonals, so it can capture either.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the black pawn on c5 can move to.
hints: Can a pawn move onto the square straight ahead if a piece stands there?
Now check the two diagonal squares ahead of the pawn.
The knight blocks the forward step, but the pawn can capture the rook on b4 and the bishop on d4.
items.explain: The knight on c4 blocks the pawn and cannot be captured, because pawns only capture diagonally. The rook on b4 and the bishop on d4 are on the pawn's forward diagonals, so it can capture either.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the black pawn on g7 can move to.
hints: The pawn is on its starting square, so look at both squares ahead of it.
The jump needs both squares empty. Is g5 empty?
Only the single step to g6 is allowed.
items.explain: The jump to g5 is blocked because the knight stands there, so only the single step to g6 works. Nothing stands on a forward diagonal, so there are no captures.

items.prompt: The black rook on h4 attacks the square e4. Can the white pawn on e2 still jump to e4? Predict, then check.
hints: Ask only the forward question: are e3 and e4 both empty?
The rules of movement do not ask whether a square is attacked.
The jump is legal, but the rook could take the pawn afterwards.
items.explain: e3 and e4 are empty, so the pawn may jump. The rook on h4 attacks e4, so the pawn could be captured next, but that is a separate question from whether the jump is legal.

items.prompt: White to move. Name the piece on g1 first, then tap every square it can move to.
hints: Is this a pawn? Check the shape. A knight has its own jumping rule.
A knight jumps in an L shape and does not need the squares between to be empty.
The knight can go to e2, to h3, and capture the pawn on f3.
items.explain: The piece on g1 is a knight, not a pawn. It can reach e2 and h3 with its L-shaped jump, and it can capture the black pawn on f3.

items.prompt: Black to move in a real opening position. Tap every square the black pawn on c5 can move to.
hints: Which colour is the pawn, and has it moved already?
It has moved, so there is no jump. Look at one step ahead and at both diagonals.
It can step to c4 or capture the pawn on d4.
items.explain: The pawn on c5 has already moved, so it can only step one square, to c4. The white pawn on d4 stands on one of its forward diagonals, so it can capture it.

items.prompt: Black to move in a real opening position. How many moves does the black pawn on e5 have? Predict, then check.
hints: Which way do black pawns walk, and what stands on the square ahead of e5?
Pawns cannot capture straight ahead.
Check both diagonal squares below e5: are they empty?
items.explain: The white pawn on e4 stands directly in front of the black pawn on e5 and cannot be captured by it. Both diagonal squares, d4 and f4, are empty, so the pawn has no move.

items.prompt: White to move. Can the piece on g4 capture the piece on g5?
hints: Look at where the rook stands compared with the pawn.
A pawn captures one square diagonally forward.
The rook is straight ahead; the knight on h5 is the piece the pawn can take.
items.explain: The rook stands straight ahead of the pawn, and pawns never capture straight ahead. The knight on h5 is on the diagonal, so that is the capture the pawn has.

items.prompt: White to move. Tap every square the piece on a2 can move to.
hints: Is the square straight ahead empty?
A pawn on the edge has only one diagonal.
It can capture the pawn on b3 and nothing else.
items.explain: The knight on a3 blocks the pawn, so there is no step and no jump. The pawn on the edge has one forward diagonal, and an enemy pawn stands there on b3.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the piece on a7 can move to.
hints: Check the colour of the pawn first.
It has not moved yet. How many squares can it go?
Two forward squares are empty, and the rook on b6 can be captured.
items.explain: The black pawn is on its starting square, so it can step to a6 or jump to a5. The white rook on b6 stands on its one forward diagonal, so it can capture it.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the piece on f7 can move to.
hints: Name the piece and its colour, then ask the forward question and the diagonal question.
The pawn is on its starting square. Both squares ahead are empty.
Two steps ahead and two captures: four squares in all.
items.explain: The pawn can step to f6 or jump to f5, and it can capture the knight on e6 or the bishop on g6. The bishop attacking the pawn does not stop it from moving.
